title: Device Streaming and Android skills - available in Android CLI
key_facts: Google updated Android CLI, its command-line tool that AI agents and other tools use to create, build, test and manage Android projects.
New: Android Device Streaming lets an agent use real physical devices remotely, as if plugged in over USB, over a secure ADB over SSL connection.
Through the terminal an agent can start devices, deploy builds, collect logs and traces, and take screenshots.
Google says its Android skills repository, structured SKILL.md instruction files that give agents official Android guidance, now has over 20 skills and that all skills are evaluated.
A new Wear Compose Material 3 skill covers Wear OS (smartwatch) app design.
Google says the skills work with Android Studio, Antigravity and third-party agents such as Claude and Codex.
Google quotes FotMob's Android tech lead saying one skill let the team migrate eight lists in an afternoon; the article says the changes compiled and were checked on an emulator.
quote_evidence: Android Device Streaming gives you access to real physical devices, remotely.
Android skills are structured instructions (SKILL.md files) that ground AI agents with our official guidance from developer.android.com.
Skills are designed to be environment-agnostic.
why_it_matters_hint: Lets AI coding agents test Android apps on real hardware without the developer owning each device, and adds guidance files so agents follow Google's current advice.
event_date: 2 Oct 2026 (feed date for the Android Developers Blog post)
notes: Official Google blog post, so the benefits and the FotMob result are Google's own selected evidence. Pool source label was blog.google; the link is the Android Developers Blog.
